object.title: Proper-source death conjecture for network attractors
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a network, and call a vertex $i$ a **proper source** if it has no incoming edges and is not isolated in the relevant network. An **attractor** is a dynamical attractor of the network, and a neuron is active in an attractor if it participates in that attractor's activity. Proper sources always die and are never active in an attractor of a network.

**Proper-source death conjecture.** Proper sources always die and are never active in an attractor of a network.

The source gives examples in which a proper source is absent from the global attractor and notes that proper sources do not participate in fixed-point supports. The general claim about all attractors remains open in the supplied text.
object.source_name: Katherine Morrison and Carina Curto, “Predicting neural network dynamics via graphical analysis”, arXiv:1804.01487 (2018).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.01487

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2018).

object.title: The combinatorial Stiefel map determines linkage matching fields
object.statement:
Let a linkage matching field be a collection of matchings satisfying the linkage conditions, and let its maximal tope linkage covectors be the maximal covectors associated to its topes. The **combinatorial Stiefel map** associates to each such covector a transversal matroid.

**Stiefel-map determination conjecture.** A linkage matching field is determined by the collection of transversal matroids associated to its maximal tope linkage covectors by the combinatorial Stiefel map.

This conjecture proposes that the transversal matroids obtained from maximal tope linkage covectors retain enough information to recover the entire linkage matching field. The source gives no resolution or evidence establishing the claim.
object.source_name: Georg Loho and Ben Smith, “Matching fields and lattice points of simplices”, arXiv:1804.01595 (2020).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.01595

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2018).

object.title: Higher-dimensional grid graph conjecture for neighborhood-prime labelings
object.statement:
For positive integers $n_1,ldots,n_t$, let $P_{n_i}$ denote the path graph on $n_i$ vertices, and let $times$ denote the Cartesian product of graphs. The graph

$$
P_{n_1}times P_{n_2}times cdots times P_{n_t}
$$

is a higher-dimensional grid graph.

**Higher-dimensional grid conjecture.** The graph $P_{n_1}times P_{n_2}times cdots times P_{n_t}$ is neighborhood-prime.

The paper proves the claim for two-dimensional grids and for three-dimensional grids whose order is divisible by $4$. It proposes the conjecture as an extension to all higher-dimensional grids; no resolution is given.
object.source_name: John Asplund, N. Bradley Fox and Arran Hamm, “New Perspectives on Neighborhood-Prime Labelings of Graphs”, arXiv:1804.02473 (2018).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.02473

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2018).

object.title: Hamiltonian edge-density conjecture for neighborhood-prime graphs
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a Hamiltonian graph of order $n$, meaning that $G$ contains a cycle through all $n$ vertices.

**Hamiltonian edge-density conjecture.** If

$$
|E(G)|>n+\frac{n}{3},
$$

then $G$ is neighborhood-prime.

The paper proves stronger sufficient conditions in some settings, including a bound derived from Hamiltonian chords, and notes that the conjecture is motivated by known results for Hamiltonian graphs of orders not congruent to $2$ modulo $4$. Its resolution is not given.
object.source_name: John Asplund, N. Bradley Fox and Arran Hamm, “New Perspectives on Neighborhood-Prime Labelings of Graphs”, arXiv:1804.02473 (2018).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.02473

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2018).

object.title: Neighborhood-prime conjecture for unions of cycles with one arbitrary component
object.statement:
For positive integers $k_1,\ldots,k_\ell$ and a positive integer $n$, let $C_m$ denote the cycle graph of length $m$, and let $\cup$ denote disjoint union.

**Cycle-union conjecture.** The union

$$
C_{4k_1}\cup C_{4k_2}\cup\cdots\cup C_{4k_\ell}\cup C_n
$$

is neighborhood-prime if $n\equiv 0\pmod{4}$ or if $n$ is odd.

The conjecture is presented as a consequence that would follow from an affirmative solution of the Deretsky–Lee–Miller prime-labeling conjecture, together with the paper's neighborhood-graph theorem. The source does not report a resolution.
object.source_name: John Asplund, N. Bradley Fox and Arran Hamm, “New Perspectives on Neighborhood-Prime Labelings of Graphs”, arXiv:1804.02473 (2018).

object.title: The centrosymmetric growth-rate inequality for permutation classes
object.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a permutation class. Write $\overline{\operatorname{gr}}(\mathcal{C})$ for its upper growth rate and $\overline{\operatorname{gr}}^{rc}(\mathcal{C})$ for the upper $rc$-growth rate, obtained from the even-size centrosymmetric permutations in $\mathcal{C}$. **Centrosymmetric growth-rate conjecture.**

$$
\overline{\operatorname{gr}}^{rc}(\mathcal{C})\leq\overline{\operatorname{gr}}(\mathcal{C}).
$$

The conjecture asserts that the growth of even-size centrosymmetric elements cannot exceed the overall growth of the class. The paper proves the reverse inequality in several settings, including sum-closed $rc$-invariant classes and certain geometric grid classes, but the general inequality remains open.
object.source_name: Justin M. Troyka, “On the centrosymmetric permutations in a class”, arXiv:1804.03686 (2019).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.03686

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2018).

object.title: The sum-closed centrosymmetric growth-rate equality conjecture
object.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a sum-closed and $rc$-invariant permutation class. Let $\operatorname{gr}(\mathcal{C})$ denote its growth rate and $\operatorname{gr}^{rc}(\mathcal{C})$ the growth rate of its even-size centrosymmetric elements, when the latter exists. **Sum-closed centrosymmetric growth-rate conjecture.** The $rc$-growth rate exists and

$$
\operatorname{gr}^{rc}(\mathcal{C})=\operatorname{gr}(\mathcal{C}).
$$

The paper proves the inequality $\underline{\operatorname{gr}}^{rc}(\mathcal{C})\geq\operatorname{gr}(\mathcal{C})$ for such classes; this conjecture would follow from the general centrosymmetric growth-rate inequality and remains open.
object.source_name: Justin M. Troyka, “On the centrosymmetric permutations in a class”, arXiv:1804.03686 (2019).

object.title: Deloera–Haws–Köppe conjecture for matroid polytopes
object.statement:
Let $M$ be a matroid on $[d]:=\{1,\ldots,d\}$, with bases $\mathcal{B}$, and let

$$
P(M):=\operatorname{conv}\left(\sum_{i\in B}{\boldsymbol{e}}_i:B\in\mathcal{B}\right)\subset\mathbb{R}^d
$$

be its matroid polytope. A lattice polytope is **Ehrhart positive** if all coefficients of its Ehrhart polynomial are positive, and **Ehrhart unimodal** if its Ehrhart $h^\ast$-polynomial has a unimodal coefficient sequence.

**Deloera–Haws–Köppe conjecture.** For any matroid $M$, the matroid polytope $P(M)$ is both Ehrhart positive and Ehrhart unimodal.

Both aspects of this conjecture were described as elusive, with only partial results known; the conjecture concerns a broad family beyond the zonotopes already known to have both properties.
object.source_name: Fu Liu and Liam Solus, “On the Relationship Between Ehrhart Unimodality and Ehrhart Positivity”, arXiv:1804.08258 (2018).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.08258

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2018).

object.title: Finch's even-term conjecture for two-generator Ulam sequences
object.statement: Let $a,b$ be relatively prime positive integers, with one of $a,b$ even. For an Ulam sequence $\mathcal{U}(a,b)$, **Finch's even-term conjecture.** If $a$ is even, then $\mathcal{U}(a,b)$ has $2+a/2$ even terms, precisely $\{a,a+2b,\ldots,a+ab,(2a+4)b\}$; if $b$ is even, then it has $2+b/2$ even terms, precisely $\{b,b+2a,\ldots,b+ba,(2b+4)a\}$. Earlier results in the paper establish lower bounds and the initial families of even terms; the source presents Finch's assertion as an open conjecture.
object.source_name: Borys Kuca, “Structures in Additive Sequences”, arXiv:1804.09594 (2018).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.09594

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2018). “We summarize his results and our observations, as well as present open questions concerning these sequences.”

object.title: Bounded subcover conjecture for sunflower-free set systems
object.statement:
Let $k$ be an integer, and let $\cal F$ be a **sunflower-free** $k$-uniform set system, meaning that it contains no sunflower with the relevant number of petals.

**Bounded subcover conjecture.** There exist $F_1,\ldots,F_{2k}\in\cal F$ such that

$$
\bigcup_{F\in\cal F}F=\bigcup_{j=1}^{2k}F_j.
$$

The source presents this as a weaker version of the preceding union-size conjecture. No resolution is given in the source.
object.source_name: Gábor Hegedűs, “About sunflowers”, arXiv:1804.10050 (2018).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.10050

object.title: The geometric griddability and finite-letter-graph conjecture
object.statement:
Let $X$ be a class of permutations, and let ${\cal G}_X$ be the corresponding class of permutation graphs. A permutation class is **geometrically griddable** when it can be represented by a geometric grid class.

**Geometric griddability and finite-letter-graph conjecture.** $X$ is geometrically griddable if and only if ${\cal G}_X$ is a class of $k$-letter graphs for some finite value of $k$.

This conjecture proposes that geometric grid classes of permutations and finite-letter graphs describe the same underlying structure through permutation graphs. The paper establishes constructive polynomial-time recognition for $3$-letter graphs, but the conjectured equivalence is not stated as resolved here.
object.source_name: Bogdan Alecu, Vadim Lozin, Dominique de Werra and Viktor Zamaraev, “Letter graphs and geometric grid classes of permutations: characterization and recognition”, arXiv:1804.11217 (2018).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.11217

object.title: The even-order non-uniform diversity conjecture
object.statement:
Let $n=2k$ and let $\mathcal{F}\subset2^{[n]}$ be intersecting. Define

$$
\operatorname{div}(\mathcal{F})=|\mathcal{F}|-\max_{x\in[n]}|\{F\in\mathcal{F}:x\in F\}|.
$$

**Even-order diversity conjecture.** If $k$ is not a power of $2$, then

$$
\operatorname{div}(\mathcal{F})\le\frac12\binom{2k-1}{k-1}+\binom{2k-1}{k+1}+\cdots+\binom{2k-1}{2k-1};
$$

and if $k$ is a power of $2$, then

$$
\operatorname{div}(\mathcal{F})\le\frac12\left(\binom{2k-1}{k-1}-1\right)+\binom{2k-1}{k+1}+\cdots+\binom{2k-1}{2k-1}.
$$

This conjecture addresses the non-uniform diversity problem in the even case, where the middle-level $k$-sets require a regular intersecting subfamily and the possible extremal value depends on whether $k$ is a power of $2$.
object.source_name: Hao Huang, “Two extremal problems on intersecting families”, arXiv:1804.11269 (2018).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.11269

object.title: Casselgren–Toft's cyclic interval coloring conjecture for biregular graphs
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a bipartite graph in which every vertex in one part has degree $a$ and every vertex in the other part has degree $b$; such a graph is called **$(a,b)$-biregular**. A cyclic interval $k$-coloring is a proper edge coloring with colors arranged cyclically so that the colors incident with each vertex form a cyclic interval.

**Casselgren–Toft's conjecture.** Every $(a,b)$-biregular graph admits a cyclic interval $\max\{a,b\}$-coloring.

Regular bipartite graphs have cyclic interval colorings, and this conjecture asks whether the corresponding optimal number of colors always exists for biregular graphs. The source cites further work for information about its status, but the supplied text does not establish a resolution.
object.source_name: C. J. Casselgren and Petros A. Petrosyan, “Some results on the palette index of graphs”, arXiv:1805.00260 (2019).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.00260

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2018).

object.title: Bottom-tree invariance of rectification in d-complete posets
object.statement:
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a $d$-complete poset with bottom tree $\mathcal{B}$. Let $T$ be a skew increasing $\mathcal{P}$-tableau, and let $R$ and $S$ be rectifications of $T$. **Bottom-tree rectification conjecture.** The restrictions of the rectifications to the bottom tree agree:

$$
R|_{\mathcal{B}}=S|_{\mathcal{B}}.
$$

This generalizes the proved unique-rectification result for chained double-tailed diamond posets and provides additional experimental evidence toward the broader unique-rectification-target conjecture. It asserts invariance on the bottom tree even when the full rectification need not yet be known to be unique.
object.source_name: Rahul Ilango, Oliver Pechenik and Michael Zlatin, “Unique rectification in d-complete posets: towards the K-theory of Kac-Moody flag varieties”, arXiv:1805.02287 (2018).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.02287

object.title: Geelen–Gerards–Whittle conjecture on branch-width under circuit-hyperplane relaxation
object.statement: Let $M_1$ be a matroid with a **circuit-hyperplane** $H$, and let $M_2$ be obtained from $M_1$ by relaxing $H$. If both $M_1$ and $M_2$ are representable over a finite field $\mathbb F$, then the branch-width of $M_1$ should be bounded by a constant depending only upon $|\mathbb F|$. This conjecture is the second conjecture used in the reported proof of Rota's Conjecture, and the paper's main result shows that it implies the corresponding fragile-matroid branch-width conjecture. The source reports that its proof was also reported by Geelen, Gerards, and Whittle.
object.source_name: Jim Geelen and Florian Hoersch, “Matroid fragility and relaxations of circuit hyperplanes”, arXiv:1805.03263 (2019).

object.title: The path-graph invariant-subspace completeness conjecture
object.statement: Let $G=P_n$ be the path graph on $n$ cells, and let $\mathcal D_{G,\ell}$ denote the collection of transformations whose invariant subspaces are being classified by the algorithm in the preceding example. **Path-graph completeness conjecture.** The algorithm in the previous example gives all of the $\mathcal D_{G,\ell}$-invariant subspaces for the path $G=P_n$. This conjecture asserts completeness of the proposed classification algorithm for invariant subspaces of path networks; the source provides no resolution.

object.title: 3-type realization conjecture for homogeneous finite-dimensional permutation structures
object.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a homogeneous finite-dimensional permutation structure, and call it **fully generic** when it is the generic structure obtained from the relevant amalgamation class.

**3-type realization conjecture.** If $\Gamma$ realizes all 3-types, then $\Gamma$ is fully generic.

This is presented as one part of the Primitivity Conjecture and is retained for consideration via direct amalgamation arguments; the source gives no resolution.
object.source_name: Samuel Braunfeld, “Infinite Limits of Finite-Dimensional Permutation Structures, and their Automorphism Groups: Between Model Theory and Combinatorics”, arXiv:1805.04219 (2018).

object.title: 3-type extension conjecture for primitive homogeneous finite-dimensional permutation structures
object.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a primitive homogeneous finite-dimensional permutation structure. A **realized 2-type** is a 2-type realized in $\Gamma$, and a 3-type involves such a 2-type when its restriction to a pair is realized in $\Gamma$.

**3-type extension conjecture.** All 3-types involving realized 2-types are realized in $\Gamma$.

This is presented as the second part of the Primitivity Conjecture; the source gives no resolution.
object.source_name: Samuel Braunfeld, “Infinite Limits of Finite-Dimensional Permutation Structures, and their Automorphism Groups: Between Model Theory and Combinatorics”, arXiv:1805.04219 (2018).

object.title: Homogeneity of equivalence classes after naming another class
object.statement:
Let $E$ be a $\emptyset$-definable equivalence relation in a finite-dimensional permutation structure, and let $C_1$ and $C_2$ be $E$-classes. Naming $C_1$ means expanding the structure by a predicate for $C_1$.

**Homogeneity-after-naming conjecture.** The class $C_2$ remains homogeneous after naming $C_1$.

The statement is identified as a possible route to ruling out counterexamples to the conjectural classification and is known in the case of three linear orders; the general claim remains open.
object.source_name: Samuel Braunfeld, “Infinite Limits of Finite-Dimensional Permutation Structures, and their Automorphism Groups: Between Model Theory and Combinatorics”, arXiv:1805.04219 (2018).

object.title: Fan–Raspaud adjacent-edge multiplicity conjecture
object.statement:
Let $G$ be a bridgeless cubic graph, let $e$ and $f$ be adjacent edges, and let $i,j$ be integers satisfying $0\leq i,j\leq 2$ and $1\leq i+j\leq 3$. An **FR-triple** is a list $C=(F_1,F_2,F_3)$ of perfect matchings with $F_1\cap F_2\cap F_3=\emptyset$, and let $\nu_C(e)$ denote the number of members of $C$ containing $e$.

**Adjacent-edge multiplicity conjecture.** The graph $G$ contains an FR-triple $C$ such that

$$
\nu_C(e)=i\qquad\text{and}\qquad\nu_C(f)=j.
$$

This is the second conjecture considered in the paper, prescribing multiplicities on two adjacent edges. The source does not give evidence that it has been resolved.
object.source_name: Vahan V. Mkrtchyan and Gagik N. Vardanyan, “On two consequences of Berge-Fulkerson conjecture”, arXiv:1805.06828 (2018).
